newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Indosuez appoints new Australian chief.
newsitem.headline: Indosuez appoints new Australian chief.

text.p: Banque Indosuez said it has appointed Don Parsonage as managing director and senior country officer of its Australian merchant bank subsidiary, Indosuez Australia Ltd.

The appointment of Parsonage marks the completion of the refocussing of the bank's Australia operations on project and export finance, real estate and selected corporate banking opportunities following the recent purchase of Banque Indosuez by Credit Agricole of France, it said.
"Project and real estate is a sector in which the bank is recognised and respected as a competitor," Parsonage said.
"It forms a substantial part of its Australian business base," he said in a statement.

The restructuring of its business in Australia was part of a new strategy which targets Asia as a key region for growth, with the overall objective of positioning the company as a leading integrated merchant bank in the region.

"It forms an integral part of the bank's global plan to refocus on core activities and markets, improve productivity and maximise efficiency in the provision of services to its clients," Parsonage said.

The bank's Australian operations have received approvals for 18 transactions totalling A$1.25 billion since July 1996, predominately in the infrastructure, energy and telecommunications sectors in both Australia and Asia.

"Notably we are currently acting as lead arranger in the winning consortium for the Loy Yang A power station. This will most likely be the largest project finance transaction anywhere in the world in 1997," Parsonage added.
